freezeAuthorization: Root authorized historical reveal after the Solver revision and independent QA were frozen.

comparisons.rootCause: MATCH: runtime objectMode behavior is delegated correctly to fast-glob, but the public async and sync declarations expose only string-array returns and lack a literal-true overload.
comparisons.behavior: MATCH: both revisions export fast-glob's Entry type and place literal objectMode:true overloads before the broad string-returning signatures. Default and false modes remain string arrays. Replay additionally records unchanged stream compatibility and verifies existing runtime entry behavior.
comparisons.tests: REPLAY STRONGER: accepted adds two TSD assertions for async and sync literal-true calls. Replay adds those plus explicit false-mode and stream assertions, two runtime tests, and independent QA for inline and reusable const options, async/sync/stream entry shapes, and default/false strings.
comparisons.scope: FUNCTIONALLY EQUIVALENT, SLIGHTLY BROADER: accepted changes index.d.ts and index.test-d.ts only (15 insertions, 3 deletions). Replay changes those files plus test.js (39 insertions, 5 deletions) to satisfy runtime-evidence acceptance. Runtime implementation is untouched in both.
comparisons.simplicity: Both use overloads and an Entry alias. Accepted expresses the sync overload as an intersection and narrows options inline with GlobbyOptions & {objectMode:true}; replay uses a named ObjectModeOptions interface and callable overload object. The replay is more verbose but readable and semantically equivalent under TSD/QA.
comparisons.regressions: No observed regression. Runtime AVA, repository and independent TSD, XO under a compatible Node runtime, whitespace, default/false behavior, literal-true const options and stream compatibility pass. No build artifact exists at this snapshot.

acceptedComparison.semanticRelationship: Equivalent overload behavior with a named public ObjectModeOptions interface in replay versus accepted inline intersection types.

limitations: The replay exposes an additional public ObjectModeOptions interface not present in the accepted patch; this is harmless in tested use but is a larger declaration surface.
The historical self-referential development dependency and old Node tooling required documented installation/runtime accommodations.
Node 24.19.0 and compatible Node 16.20.2 on Linux were exercised, not the full historical Node matrix.
The snapshot has no build script; build is correctly NOT_APPLICABLE rather than PASS.
